rationale: The Latin anchors *dealbari* ("to be whitened/made white") and *micare* ("to shine, glitter, flash") — as seen in the Psalm contexts ("super nivem dealbabor" = "I shall be whiter than snow"; "in justitia apparebo [micabo]" = "I shall shine/appear in justice") — clearly point to a sense of shining, gleaming, or becoming brilliantly white, not to causing wonder or bewilderment. Neither candidate synset (amaze.v.01 "affect with wonder" nor perplex.v.01 "be bewildering to") captures the core physical/visual sense of *a-blican* ("to shine, gleam, be white/bright"). The English gloss token "amaze" here appears to be an archaic or poetic usage meaning "to dazzle with brightness" (cf. Middle English *amasen* with senses of stunning brilliance), which has no direct WordNet analog.
